facts.text: The film opens by claiming to be "Based on a true story..." It isn't, as far as anyone can tell, but it's a classic grindhouse hook.
Hack-O-Lantern was filmed in 1986 but didn't reach audiences until 1988, two years later.
Grandpa is played by Hy Pyke, who was born Monty Pike. The character actor spent decades playing weirdos and heavies in low-budget and cult films.
Katina Garner, who plays mother Amanda, also turned up in the Roller Blade (1986) and the cult comedy Wacko (1982), and in A Polish Vampire in Burbank (1983).
Director Jag Mundhra was Indian-born. Hack-O-Lantern was only his second Hollywood film, after the slasher Open House (1987).
Grandpa star Hy Pyke is also Taffey Lewis, the sleazy club owner in Ridley Scott's Blade Runner (1982), as Paste Magazine's Jim Vorel points out.
Paste Magazine's Jim Vorel called Hy Pyke's Grandpa performance the film's highlight, a drawl-and-lisp mix that turns sinister lines unintentionally funny.
On Tubi, the closed captions for Hack-O-Lantern sometimes read "SPEAKING GIBBERISH" or go blank when Grandpa (Hy Pyke) screams, Paste Magazine's Jim Vorel noticed.
Grandpa actor Hy Pyke died on October 26, 2006, five days before Halloween.
The Rifftrax crew mocked Hack-O-Lantern on October 28, 2022, just in time for Halloween.
Hy Pyke once had a small part in John Milius' gangster film Dillinger (1973) that was cut out. He also played Bebe Rebozo in an unreleased Nixon satire.
Hysteria Lives says the film looks like it was shot through a soft, Vaseline-smeared lens, mixing slasher violence with family melodrama and some nudity.
Vera is played by Carla B., who is credited as Carla Baron in some listings.
Teenage Tommy is meant to be 18, but actor Gregory Scott Cummins looks about 30, according to Paste Magazine's Jim Vorel.
The song "Devil's Son" was performed by D.C. La Croix, written by Slyvie LaCroix and distributed by EMI. It's the film's heavy-metal theme.
The killer's mask is a store-bought Halloween mask called Hooded Fear, designed by Bill Ystrom for Be Something Studio. The production added paint and hair.
Goof: the cashier says Nora's total is $40, and gives $15 change for one bill. That would make it a $55 bill.
Nora, the girl in the pool, is played by Jeanna Fine, an adult film star credited here as Angel Rush.
Watch Nora's pentagram tattoo: it nearly washes off after she leaves the pool, then returns upside-down after she drops her towel. It was just paint.
Tommy's bunker is decked out with an Elvira poster, a Killian's Irish Red beer sign and heavy metal cassettes. It fits a film that nods to Elvira's Movie Macabre.
Tommy's shrine includes an upside-down cross as a Satanic symbol. It's a movie cliche. The inverted cross is traditionally linked to St. Peter, who asked to be crucified upside-down.
Tommy actor Gregory Scott Cummins was named best punter in University of Hawaii football history on its 40-year all-star team in 1991.
Director Jag Mundhra (1948-2011) is best known for his early career as an American exploitation writer-director, before returning to Indian cinema.
Star Gregory Scott Cummins claims director Jag Mundhra couldn't speak English. Co-star Marya Gant says Mundhra held a US marketing master's degree, per DVD Exotica's Massacre Video review.
Hack-O-Lantern is also known under the alternate title Halloween Night.
The film got a second life when RedLetterMedia featured it on episode 58 of their "Best of the Worst" series, introducing it to a new generation.
Hack-O-Lantern was shot on 35mm film. DVD Exotica reviewed the Massacre Video release and thought it looked far more professional than fans previously believed.
Hack-O-Lantern gets a shout-out in the 1988 Dirty Harry sequel The Dead Pool. It's also referenced in WNUF Halloween Special (2013).
Massacre Video's 2017 disc was billed as the first legit release since VHS. Before that, fans relied on smudgy fullscreen tapes and rips.
TMDB lists the film's budget at $5.5 million.
Hysteria Lives counts 8 bodies in Hack-O-Lantern, 4 women and 4 men, killed by a hammer claw, shovel, rake, tightened corset, strangulation and a gunshot.
Goof: Brian is pulled out of the grave, and his chest is visibly still breathing.
Richard Scheib of Moria called the rock-band dream sequence, with its fake-looking severed head, the film's most ridiculous element. He gave the movie one star.
Paste Magazine's Jim Vorel described the Halloween party's stand-up comedian routine as painfully awkward. The party also features strippers, and a woman dancing with a boa constrictor.
In 2021 the film was a case on TV's The People's Court. Massacre Video, who released its Blu-ray, sued someone who uploaded it to YouTube.
Director Jag Mundhra's daughter, Smriti Mundhra, grew up to be an Academy Award-nominated director and producer, according to his Wikipedia page.
Tommy actor Gregory Scott Cummins later played Mac's dad on It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia and appeared in Cliffhanger (1993).
The film nods to horror hits like Halloween (1978) and Silver Bullet (1985). The Blu-ray release calls the film a Halloween-night slasher.
Reviewer at Movies and Drinks recalls his school changed its "Demons" mascot to "Dolphins" around 1987-88, the Satanic panic era that Hack-O-Lantern was made in.
